title: Resilience Lab: Standup & Handoff Notes — 2029-05-18
content:
TL;DR:
- Midweek resilience lab check-in. Short on-call window: 09:00–10:30 PT handoff today.
- One SEV-2 incident (INC-2029-113) this week related to canary-to-default model routing thrash during a region scale event; mitigations applied, follow-up assigned.
- SLOs: overall text-generation availability 99.85% (7d rolling) — slightly below the 99.9% target due to the incident; token-latency p95 drifted to 420ms for 1 hour during canary roll.
- Action items: backfill canary health gating, add early fallback for quantized variants, tune autoscaler cooldowns, refine on-call runbook for routing stalls.

Standup notes (2029-05-18, 09:00 PT)
Attendees: Asha (chair), Miguel, Oliver, Renee, on-call: Kevin L. (night)->Mina R. (day)
Agenda: incident recap, SLO health, ongoing experiments, handoff checklist, blockers.

1) Incident recap: INC-2029-113 (SEV-2) — Canary routing thrash
- Timeline: 2029-05-16 03:12 UTC first observed error spike; full mitigation by 2029-05-16 04:08 UTC.
- Symptom: Canary instances reported short TCP stalls when routing table switched from region-eu to region-us-east during a transient capacity rebalancing. Result: request retries + cascading fallback to default model variant, increased token latency and some 5xxs.
- Root-cause hypothesis: timing window in the smart-router's transient policy where in-flight requests lost a routing key (race between KV-cache invalidation and prefix caching).
- Immediate mitigations applied: 1) disabled canary autoscale burst for the affected pool; 2) forced graceful drain (30s) for router workers during routing updates; 3) temporary raise of canary health threshold to 99.98% for rollout gating.
- Post-incident action owners: Miguel -> SRE-7421 (add gating + metric), Oliver -> runtime PR (see linked PR) to add request pinning during routing table changes, Renee -> update runbook and communicate to infra-scheduling.

2) SLO / metrics snapshot (7d rolling window at time of note)
- Text generation availability: 99.85% (target 99.9%) — burn primarily from INC-2029-113 (0.06% loss).
- Token p95 latency (production, text-gen-default): 190ms baseline, spike to 420ms for 1h during incident.
- Inference error rate (5xx): baseline 0.02%, peaked to 0.9% during incident.
- Burn rate: 3.2x for the 1h window. Forecast: if similar events recur weekly, SLA risk increases — need gates.

3) Ongoing experiments and results
- KV-cache warmers (experimental): early results show reduced cold-start latency for long prefix reuse patterns; however, warming adds CPU pressure. Miguel to present microbench numbers next week.
- Dynamic quantization pilot on small model slice: slightly higher CPU efficiency but a small (0.2%) increase in misaligned token outputs for edge prompts. Evaluating trade-offs.
- Autoscaler cooldown tuning: current cooldown 60s; proposal to move to 90s during canary bursts to avoid thrash. A/B planned next Tuesday (SRE-7430).

4) On-call handoff notes (critical items to pass on to next shift)
- Watch for new canary rollouts (tags: canary/auto, canary/manual) — avoid manual promotions without gating metrics green for 30m.
- If router errors >0.5% sustained for 5m: route to fallback variant and pause canaries (runbook step 3).
- If token p95 > 350ms for >10m and burn rate >2x: initiate traffic-shed policy to non-critical tiers and notify product-impact channel.
- Contact list: infra-pager, runtime-oncall Slack channel, Mina R. (day on-call), Kevin L. (night handoff).

5) Action items (owners / ETA)
- SRE-7421 (Miguel) — add canary gating metric and dashboard, ETA: 2029-05-24.
- Runtime PR (Oliver) — request pinning patch for routing updates, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284, review requested, ETA: 2029-05-21.
- Runbook update (Renee) — add explicit steps for routing-table change and a quick triage checklist, ETA: 2029-05-20.
- Autoscaler tuning experiment (Asha + SRE) — run A/B with 90s cooldown on canary pools, start 2029-05-21, initial result check 2029-05-28.
- Postmortem draft (owner: Kevin L.) — collect logs, spans, and trace slices; initial draft by 2029-05-22.

6) Handoff checklist (for Mina R. incoming day-shift)
- Review INC-2029-113 postmortem draft link in linked_artifacts.
- Verify canary pools: region-eu and region-us-east have no manual promotions scheduled this morning.
- Confirm the temporary canary health threshold remains at 99.98% until SRE-7421 gating is live; revert only after confirmatory tests.
- Run quick smoke test: issue 50 short text-gen requests across 3 regions, verify p95 < 220ms and zero 5xxs.
- Update on-call diary with any anomalies; escalate to product if customer-facing error spike.

7) Blockers and open questions
- How much headroom do we need to safely operate KV-cache warmers in production? (CPU/mem budget). Miguel to quantify.
- Quantization pilot: what is acceptable quality delta before we block rollout? Product input needed.
- Do we need an automated canary rollback trigger based on router error ratio vs token-latency slope? Proposal: design in SRE-7509.

8) Notes from the trenches (observations)
- Several teams reported noisy alerts during the region rebalance window; suggestion to add a transient-suppression tag for planned infra operations.
- Developer feedback: clearer canary labeling (metadata:version+commit+region) reduces confusion during cross-team incident response.

Next meeting: 2029-05-25 09:00 PT (Resilience Lab midweek).

Appendix: quick links and logs
- INC-2029-113 ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-2029-113
- SRE-7421 (gating dashboard): https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-7421
- Runtime patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Trace span dump (S3): s3://redwood-ops/traces/2029/05/16/inc-113-tracedump.json

Notes to self: keep handoff terse, always include immediate mitigations and owners. This doc is intentionally light on formal postmortem prose — see postmortem draft in linked artifacts for full timeline and RCA.
